answer: To resist Sybil attacks, require a slashable identity bond plus single-use peer vouchers. An agent locks collateral and enters a public atlas of identities; each voucher is signed by a peer it actually traded with and counts once, so a clone cannot reuse it under another name. Posing as N agents costs N bonds plus N independent vouchers, forcing the attacker to earn real cooperation instead of minting keys. If a committee links two names to one wallet, every tied bond is slashed: a fake orchard of accounts is paid for with a glacier of capital that never returns.
